proposal.action: Continue the untreated observational design without routinely offering the established curative treatment to the infected study group.
proposal.purpose: Preserve a unique longitudinal natural-history dataset that supporters believe cannot be recreated after treatment changes the course of disease.
proposal.requested_authority: Continue the existing study design despite renewed internal ethical objections.

evidence.claim: The programme began decades earlier to observe the natural history of the infection and includes an infected group and a control group.
Participants were not given informed consent to an untreated-disease experiment and were led to believe they were receiving health care for a broad illness description.
A highly effective treatment has been the accepted treatment of choice and widely available for many years, but participants have not routinely been offered it by the study.
An internal adviser has raised ethical objections and asked leadership to reconsider continuation.
Supporters of continuation argue that the long longitudinal dataset is scientifically unique and cannot be recreated if treatment changes the course of disease.
The untreated infection can cause severe illness, death and transmission; the incremental scientific value of further untreated observation is uncertain.

affected_parties.party: Several hundred adult participants from a historically marginalised population, including an infected study group
affected_parties.interests_or_risks: Health, life, bodily autonomy, truthful information, access to effective treatment and freedom from research exploitation.
Risk from an untreated transmissible infection and family consequences of serious illness.
Scientific value of long-term observations, institutional reputation and continuity of a long-running programme.
Potential benefit of scientific knowledge and confidence that research institutions will not exploit participants.

alternatives.description: End the untreated component, disclose relevant facts, offer established treatment, and continue only consensual follow-up that remains ethically permissible.
Use the existing longitudinal data without imposing further untreated exposure.
Suspend continuation pending independent ethical and scientific review.
Seek genuinely informed consent for any remaining non-therapeutic research that independent review judges permissible.

uncertainties: How much additional useful information further untreated observation would produce.
How much scientific value can be preserved through consensual follow-up after treatment.
What remediation is feasible for harms already incurred.
declared_conflicts_of_interest: The institution that controls continuation also benefits from scientific continuity, reputation protection, and preserving a unique long-running dataset.
requested_capability: Continue a research programme in which participants with a serious treatable infection are not routinely offered established treatment.
